story.title: How is a syllable built?
story.lead: Four small pieces add up to ค้าน (/kʰáːn/, “to oppose”). Here is what each one does.

initial.title: Start with a consonant
initial.body: ค sounds like /kʰ/. It belongs to the Low class, and the class decides how the tone is read later on.

vowel.title: Vowels cling around the consonant
vowel.body: า sounds like /aː/, a long vowel. In Thai a vowel can be written before, above, below or after its consonant. Here it sits on the right.

final.title: Close it with a final
final.body: น sounds like /n/ at the end. It is a sonorant, so the syllable is live, and live syllables can take every tone mark.

mark.title: Finish with a tone mark
mark.body: The mark ◌้ (mai tho) sits above the consonant. With a Low-class consonant it gives the High tone. The same mark on a Mid-class consonant gives Falling.

result.title: Four pieces, one syllable
result.body: Color shows the job of each piece. Now it is your turn to build.

ipa.howTo: Columns: where in the mouth the sound is made. Rows: how the air is released.
ipa.title: The sounds of Thai
ipa.intro: Get to know the sounds before the letters. Tap any IPA symbol to hear an example and compare it with the closest English sound.
ipa.cDesc: Arranged by place (columns) and manner (rows) of articulation. Watch the aspirated row: Thai contrasts p/pʰ, t/tʰ, k/kʰ where English doesn’t.
ipa.vTitle: 9 basic vowels, each short and long
ipa.vDesc: Position in the chart is the position of your tongue. Several of these (ɯ, ɤ) don’t exist in English.
ipa.tDesc: Same /kʰaː/ frame, 5 tones, 5 different meanings. Tap to hear and see the pitch contour.
ipa.multiClass: One sound, letters from several classes. The class doesn’t change how the consonant sounds; it decides the tone of the whole syllable.
ipa.lengthNote: Vowel length changes meaning in Thai, and it also affects tone. Dashed border = short, solid border = long; this convention is used across the site.
ipa.toneChartAria: Contours of the 5 tones on a 1–5 scale

history.title: Where Thai script comes from
history.intro: Thai is an abugida: consonants are the core and vowels attach around them. That idea has been passed down for over 2,000 years. Scroll along the main line from Brahmi to modern Thai, and glance at the grey branches to see the cousins that split off on the way.
history.kaNote: The big letter on each card is that script’s “ka”, where Unicode has one.
history.endTitle: Now you know where it comes from
history.endBody: Time to use it. Pick a consonant, a vowel and a tone mark, and build a syllable yourself.

aksornthai.title: Aksorn Thai – Thai script
aksornthai.intro: Explore the 44 consonants in traditional order and the vowel signs that combine with them. Select a letter to see its details.
aksornthai.rareHint: Pale background: rare. Struck through: obsolete.

aksornthai.practiceHint: The same letter in 4 fonts. When writing by hand, follow the looped font (มีหัว); loopless fonts (ไม่มีหัว) are common on signs.

builder.title: Build syllables
builder.intro: Pick or drag the four pieces of a syllable. Border color is the consonant class, transcription color is the tone.
builder.sumHint: Drag a piece up to the builder, or tap to choose.
builder.hoverHint: Hover or tap each box to see the process at that step.
builder.vowelNoFinal: This vowel doesn’t take a final consonant.
builder.finalLegend: Filled: sonorant (makes a live syllable). Outlined: stop (makes a dead syllable).
builder.stepsTitle: Step by step to the tone
builder.notWordBody: This syllable is spelled correctly but isn’t a common word (per the app’s dictionary). Try another tone mark, vowel or final.
builder.tableDesc: Each cell is a formula: row = consonant class, column = syllable type or tone mark. The cell used by the syllable above is highlighted.
builder.tapHint: Tap a tile to choose a piece. On a computer you can also drag and drop.

groups.leadingHint: silent ห / อ change the class
groups.diphIntro: Compound vowels (diphthongs) glide from one sound to another and are written with two or three pieces around the consonant, e.g. เ◌ีย = เ + ◌ี + ย, read /ia/.

notebook.title: Writing notebook · 4 tiers
notebook.morphed: The vowel changes shape with a final: {from} → {to}.
notebook.taikhu: The tone mark takes the place of ◌็, so ◌็ is dropped and the vowel stays short.

syllable.placement: The vowel is written {sides} the consonant {initial}.
syllable.placementBefore: Even when written first, it is read AFTER the consonant: always say {initial} first.
